items: `diff_analysis.source_filter` globs compile through the shared protocol `compileGlob` (anchored, case-insensitive); matching is unchanged for every default and documented pattern, and a double star not followed by a slash and not trailing is now a plain star, which is how git reads the emitted pathspec (`a**b` no longer crosses a slash)
A chat-suggested action can no longer target the `subtask` role: a child checklist unit is observed, never spawned, so role normalization accepts only dispatchable session roles

Child checklist units (ADR-060) are observed end to end: the task watcher follows the `subtasks/` directory beside each checklist (local) or each child file through the node (remote) and picks up a registry that already exists when it arms, `task.progress` returns the child under the step that owns it (steps completed, current step, source digests, last mark time, and a projected `stale` after 15 idle minutes), `subtasks/` travels to the slot with `assets/`, `inputs/` and `artifacts/` through one shared list and mirrors back per file as `subtasks/<name>.worker`, a terminal signal with an unsettled child is refused as an artifact-contract failure naming the unit, and each child's step count, duration and source land on `run.metrics.subtasks` and in the gate summary's per-step timing

Dispatch, tmux nudge, and warm-session handoff stage `assets/`, `inputs/`, `artifacts/` and `subtasks/` through one copy helper that skips `*.worker` files. The mirror is orchestrator-owned output written from the slot, so re-dispatching a task directory that already completed no longer puts stale copies of the worker's own files back beside the live ones

The acceptance-criteria ledger (ADR-060) reaches every client: the task watcher follows one non-recursive watch on the task's `artifacts/` directory locally, dispatching only on `acceptance-status.json` and ignoring every other artifact, and watches that file through the node remotely; either way a ledger already on disk is read once when the watch arms. A verdict broadcasts progress as it lands (a ledger write ticks no checkbox, so it bypasses the parent checkbox-hash guard and carries no child tag), and `task.progress` returns the ledger, the criteria the task registered and any read failure, so a criterion with no verdict — or an unreadable ledger — is still reported
